blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The paper implements the direct narrow-control comparison previously used in reference [5] and explicitly contrasts its null discrimination comparison with that paper’s shorter ball-ball than ball-box looking times. This is a retested finding with a new sample, despite the age difference. The evidence quote preserves the interleaved text exactly as supplied, without joining columns or repairing text.

luna_triage.reason: The Results implement the direct Narrow-Control test and report the present comparison; Discussion explicitly contrasts it with Wilcox and Baillargeon's [5] earlier ball-ball versus ball-box result. The reference list identifies [5] as the 1998 event-monitoring paper, distinct from shipped row 168 ([4], the Cognitive Psychology paper). The finding is directly retested, and no supplied shipped row represents [5].
luna_triage.location: Results, direct Narrow-Control comparison; Discussion §5.2; References [5]
luna_triage.omission_quote: The direct Narrow-Control test that we employed has been used in studies by Wilcox and her collaborators as well. For example, in their followup to the reference study, Wilcox and Baillargeon [5] obtained consistently shorter looking times in the narrow-screen ball-ball conditions (7.5-month-olds: 𝑀narrow-ball-ball = 18.5 s; SD = 11.0; 4.5-month-olds: 𝑀narrow-ball-ball = 22.9 s, SD = 9.2), relative to the narrow-screen ball-box conditions (7.5-month-olds: 𝑀narrow-ball-box = 34.2 s, SD = 8.6; 4.5-month-olds: 𝑀narrow-ball-box = 40.2 s, SD = 10.5; see also [23]).
luna_triage.identity_quote: [5] T. Wilcox and R. Baillargeon, “Object individuation in young infants: further evidence with an event-monitoring paradigm,” Developmental Science, vol. 1, no. 1, pp. 127–142, 1998.
